title: Adaptive rate controller priority-elevation loop causing silent request suppression during capacity switchover
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers (two enterprise Dedicated tenants and one Private deployment customer) reported unexplained 5xx and opaque failures during a scheduled capacity handover window. Investigation found an interaction between the adaptive-rate-controller's priority elevation feature and ephemeral routing state during switchover that resulted in silent suppression of admitted requests for lower-priority tenants. This ticket tracks the outage triage, short-term mitigations, root cause analysis, and the production fix rollout.
timeline:
2026-02-20 02:14 UTC - First alert: increased 5xxs on tenant-ACME (Dedicated).
2026-02-20 02:18 UTC - Second alert: Private customer 'FinBank' reported degraded throughput during warmup.
2026-02-20 02:22 UTC - Pager duty triggered; SRE paged.
2026-02-20 02:30 UTC - Manual rollback of recent adaptive-rate-controller config changes to previous stable flag version.
2026-02-20 03:05 UTC - Mitigation applied: disable priority elevation feature for multi-tenant handovers; traffic stabilized for most tenants.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Simulate capacity handover by triggering orchestrator node drain and reattach flows in staging.
2) Enable priority-elevation feature in adaptive-rate-controller with aggressive boost thresholds.
3) Send mixed-tenant traffic: high-rate VIP tenant + several lower-rate tenants concurrently.
4) Observe admission metrics: suppressed admission tokens and increased drop count for lower-priority tenants during switchover window.
mitigation:
Short term: rolled back priority-elevation config flag and applied a temporary guard in the orchestrator to avoid exporting 'suppress' routing hints during handover. Increased monitoring and alerted support teams.
Customer remediation: manual warmup for impacted tenants where necessary and temporary dedicated burst capacity for FinBank.
root_cause:
Two contributing defects:
1) The adaptive-rate-controller's priority-elevation logic used a per-tenant ephemeral boost token that was cached in the edge admission registry with a TTL of 60s. During orchestrator handover the registry entries were not invalidated consistently across regions, leaving stale 'boost' markers on some VIP tenant IDs while other tenant admission state was rebuilt.
2) The orchestrator's handover path emitted a transient routing hint 'suppress-lower-priority' for a 5s window which the admission layer treated as authoritative and suppressed tokens for any tenant evaluated as lower priority. Because the boost token cache persisted on a subset of nodes, the controller entered a feedback loop: boosted tenants reclaimed capacity while suppressed tenants saw no admission, causing autoscaler warmup attempts to fail and triggering opaque 5xxs.
investigation_notes:
- Correlated edge admission logs with orchestrator handover traces (trace IDs: trace-20260220-02-16-xx).
- Found mismatch between cache invalidation TTL and orchestrator handover window.
- Reproduced locally with a synthetic multi-tenant harness.
- Customer Slack escalation from FinBank CS at 02:25 UTC (see linked channel messages).
fix_plan:
1) Patch adaptive-rate-controller to treat routing hints as advisory, not authoritative, during handovers. (ENG change)
2) Ensure cache invalidation on orchestrator handoff: emit explicit cache-invalidate event and/or reduce TTL to <1s during switchover windows. (Orchestrator change)
3) Add e2e test in staging that simulates handover + mixed-tenant traffic to prevent regression. (Testing)
4) Roll out patch behind a kill-switch flag; monitor admission rate, drop count, and customer errors for 30 minutes before gating wider rollout.
rollback_plan: If the rollout causes regressions: toggle kill-switch and revert orchestrator patch quickly via the standard deploy rollback job. Fall back to previous admission controller image and confirm traffic stabilizes. Notify impacted customers and open a follow-up remediation ticket.
release_steps:
1) Merge PRs and run full CI including new e2e harness.
2) Canary deploy patches to a single region with non-production tenants.
3) Enable for Dedicated-only traffic for 30 minutes.
4) Gradual global rollout if metrics stable.
5) Post-rollout validation and close ticket.
